title: Jeremiah's Woe and God's Promise

questions.question: Then the Lord said to me, "Though... and... stood before me, yet my heart would not turn toward this people. Send them out of my sight, and let them go!"
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:1 (ESV): "Though Moses and Samuel stood before me, yet my heart would not turn toward this people."

questions.question: "And when they ask you, 'Where shall we go?' you shall say to them, 'Thus says the Lord: Those who are for..., to...; and those who are for the sword, to the sword; those who are for famine, to famine; and those who are for captivity, to captivity.'"

questions.question: "I will appoint over them four kinds of destroyers, declares the Lord: the sword to kill, the... to tear, and the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:3 (ESV): "the sword to kill, the dogs to tear, and the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy."

questions.question: Because of what king of Judah did the Lord say he would make the people a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:4 (ESV): "And I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth because of what Manasseh the son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, did in Jerusalem."

questions.question: "Who will have... on you, O Jerusalem, or who will bemoan you? Who will turn aside to ask about your welfare?"

questions.question: "Woe is me, my mother, that you bore me, a man of... and... to the whole land! I have not lent, nor have I borrowed, yet all of them curse me."

questions.question: The Lord replies: "If you utter what is precious, and not what is..., you shall be as my mouth. They shall turn to you, but you shall not turn to them."

key_verse_text: Your words were found, and I ate them, and your words became to me a joy and the delight of my heart, for I am called by your name, O Lord, God of hosts.
